# Complete Entner–Doudoroff module: external author dossier

This candidate represents **KEGG:M00008**, from beta-D-glucose 6-phosphate to D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate and pyruvate. Five reaction objects cover four positions. KEGG:R02736 and KEGG:R10907 are alternative NADP/NAD oxidations at position one, followed by RHEA:12557, RHEA:17278 and RHEA:17090. They are not serial reactions and their two branch nets are never summed. The candidate has 19 participants, 37 mechanistic edges and 92 edge-local evidence blocks. This is external authoring awaiting independent whole-record review and later canonical integration, not a scientific approval or a published record.

## Identity, novelty and full boundary

The original M00008 ENTRY/NAME/DEFINITION/ORTHOLOGY explicitly lists both oxidation reactions and the three remaining native KEGG reactions. K01057/K07404 are alternative lactonase ortholog families, not an instruction to invent a second E. coli Pgl or a physical complex. Native R10907's inverse MODULE field omits M00008; that source discrepancy is retained locally. Complete original KEGG membership is mapped in `ed-source-projection.json` and checked against the original flatfile, rather than inferred from enzyme names or order alone.

GO:0061678 covers more than this exact source-defined route, and GO:0009255 is obsolete. The native KEGG module is therefore retained. MetaCyc:ENTNER-DOUDOROFF-PWY denotes a distinct two-reaction shunt; it is neither an exact mapping nor a substitute for the complete selected module. Glucose uptake/phosphorylation, alternative gluconate entry and lower glycolysis with ATP generation remain outside the selected boundary. Both source-listed donor alternatives and every chemical side within the boundary are included.

The new search used `rg -uu --follow` in both the original Documents checkout and the prepared next-216 worktree, excluding only Git internals and the environment. Exact module/reaction/accession/primary identifiers and labels were searched. Matching existing records were read: oxidative pentose phosphate shares Zwf/Pgl/hydrolysis but proceeds to ribulose phosphate; D-galacturonate degradation shares the aldol cleavage but has a different entry route; sulfo-ED uses different sulfur substrates and scope. The old BRENDA 15-reaction canary is source research, not a complete maintained M00008 record. Source inventories, historical snapshots and generated pages were dispositioned. No complete duplicate was found within these explicitly bounded searches. Compressed archives were not unpacked by the text search; the source inventories and prior preflight assessments were separately inspected. Exact roots, commands, hashes and hit dispositions are retained in `ed-dedup.json`.

## Chemical identity and direction

Original KEGG C01172 is neutral beta-D-glucose 6-phosphate and matches ChEBI:17719's Standard InChI. Selected CHEBI:58247 is the corresponding dianion. Removing only the protonation layer preserves the full connectivity and stereochemical graph; neutral and charged entities are not asserted to be identical. CHEBI:58225 is alpha and CHEBI:61548 leaves the anomer unspecified. Neither replaces the native beta substrate, and generic Rhea:15842 is not relabeled as a beta-specific equation. Both first-position reaction nodes preserve native reversible direction, with consumption/production edges explicitly selecting the catabolic module orientation.

All twelve native compound structures were fetched as original KEGG MOL files and independently converted with RDKit, compared with the issuing ChEBI SQL InChIs after only protonation normalization. The native flatfile ATOM/BOND fields and separate MOL bodies are retained. For downstream reactions, original R02035/R02036/R05605 link bidirectional Rhea:12559/17280/17092. The full original Rhea142 RDF explicitly links those to masters 12556/17277/17089 and selected directions 12557/17278/17090. Its substrates/products, participant objects, coefficient predicates, chemical accessions, formulas and charges independently establish the exact directed sides. No direction is inferred solely from pathway order.

Every selected equation balances atoms and charge. Each separate four-position net consumes beta-G6P(2-) and its one oxidized donor, produces GAP(2-), pyruvate, reduced donor and two hydrons. Hydrolysis and dehydration water cancel. There is no ATP in this module net. The two NAD/NADP branches do not establish equal physiological use. All chemical side edges and four continuity edges have source-local evidence; the native ordering assertion is kept separate from upstream/downstream chemical identity evidence.

## Protein and experimental scope

The record taxon is E. coli K-12, and current issuing UniProt entries P0AC53, P52697, P0ADF6 and P0A955 all name taxon 83333. This current annotation scope is kept separate from historical donor strains, expression hosts and engineered constructs. The protein projection retains the complete native sequences, lengths, hashes, comments, evidence tiers and reported conflicts.

**Zwf.** The official 2012 full main text was read through the publisher's web rendering. Its Table 1 supports both NADP and NAD capacity with very different affinities. The pETG6PDH* preparation retains twelve N-terminal residues after cleavage. BL21 is an expression host, not proof of the donor strain or equality to the current 491-residue sequence. The 2016 original JATS describes a different TEV construct expected to retain Gly-His, uses engineered variants, and retains the earlier wild-type comparator. Its S1 Table row 9 identifies P0AC53 for sequence analysis; this is not a complete experimental construct sequence bridge. Current generic catalytic annotation is HAMAP/ECO:0000255. Applying supported activity to KEGG's exact beta convention is explicitly an annotation-level inference, not exclusive-anomer characterization or measured NAD-dependent in vivo ED flux. No dimer is inferred from a homology-model interface and no obligatory Mg cofactor is inferred from assay buffer.

**Pgl.** The 2004 original primary source documents deletion/complementation and extract activity, with mutations moved from DY378 to MG1655. Its assay is not fully quantitative. Current P52697 hydrolysis annotation is experimentally supported, but these data do not establish purified assembly or a bound-metal requirement.

**Edd.** Current P0ADF6 has 603 residues. The original annotation identifies PLR at positions 252–254 versus historical AC; exact older 602-residue construct equality is not claimed. The 2007 primary Methods identify K-12 PCR and BL21(DE3) expression with active lysates. Manganese supplementation during expression does not establish a mandatory bound Mn cofactor. The peroxide paper supports Edd activity loss and iron/DTT recovery. Its explicit [3Fe-4S] EPR result belongs to fumarase A, not Edd. The selected [4Fe-4S] annotation and one-cluster count retain ECO:0000250/0000255/0000305 inference distinctions. No purified Edd assembly or directly measured cluster stoichiometry is invented.

**Eda.** The original native complex has three copies of its monomer, whose original object explicitly unifies P0A955. Current UniProt states a homotrimer with experimental evidence; the 2001 full primary article independently describes recombinant trimeric structure. Its expression/SeMet host does not establish a MG1655 donor. The source-issued complex identity is used with qualified preparation scope. The coupled LDH assay detects pyruvate through NADH loss; that NADH is excluded from the Eda equation. Other Eda substrate activities are outside this exact route. Cytoplasm is retained at the current curator-inference tier, not generalized to every enzyme.

**Regulation.** The 2005 CsrA Results/Figure 7 and Discussion describe generally positive, indirect expression effects, while the section heading and current annotation say negative. The conflict and original paragraphs are retained. No direct inhibition of Eda, its reaction, or its protein activity is exported. The record does not substitute an expression observation for a causal catalytic edge.

## Expression context and access limits

The unchanged canonical iModulonDB adapter was used with fresh original responses for e_coli/precise_mg1655. Fifteen queries and four direct gene lookups led to 21 retained HTTP bodies and component 25. That component contains edd/b1851 and eda/b1850. Search hits alone are not membership; lack of another queried row in this selected component is not global biological absence. This computational context does not establish catalysis, direct regulation, donor flux or historical construct identity. Every normalized result is replayed offline from the retained originals through the same unmodified adapter.

Original bytes and exact retrieval receipts remain external. The 2012 official main text is web-inspected, but direct full-body acquisition returned HTTP 403; the rejected body/access attempt remains recorded. Its record reference deliberately has no fabricated article hash, and the offline replay does not pretend to validate inaccessible article bytes. The 2016 JATS/workbook and downstream primary articles have retained original bodies. Older abstracts and failed/challenge responses remain acquisition context only. No source-exhaustion claim is made.

## Reproduction and integration boundary

`ed-replay-final.py` uses explicit record/repository/output paths and exclusive success output. It captures formal and predecessor proof identities before imports, independently parses original source structures, primary selectors and current annotations, verifies every declared chemical side and both branch nets, validates the closed schema, and exports actual KGX evidence without loss. It rechecks original digests and formal/prior-proof identities before emitting success. Negative controls include a missing donor alternative, alpha substitution, serial alternatives, a leaked LDH reporter, changed chemical coefficient, wrong trimer stoichiometry and invented obligatory Mn. The 2012 web-only limitation remains explicit rather than being converted into a passing byte check.

`ed-authority-proposal.json` contains original input paths, URLs, kinds, hashes, exact canonical terms and a minimal source proposal. `ed-identifiers.json` distinguishes existing from missing named terms. No shared authority snapshot, identifier policy, pathway history, generated page, Git state or GitHub state was changed. Full-corpus/render/publication gates await independent review and root-owned integration. Temporary author-preparation API/locator/format failures are retained and will be listed with actual terminal results in the final handoff.
